memory_candidates.content: When a codebase already has an append-only JSONL store helper (flock'd, jq -c -n built, lazily created) and a second store needs the same treatment, check the mutability axis before assuming a literal port. An append-only log's helper needs one code path; a mutable-record store needs a second read-modify-write path with fundamentally different lock discipline: the flock must be held across the whole read -> jq transform -> temp-write -> validate -> atomic mv sequence, not just the write, and the MERGED result must be validated before the mv (validating only the delta lets a corrupt merge land). This distinction is invisible at the 'mirror the existing script' level of planning and only surfaces by reading the consumer's documented mutation workflow. A useful planning tell: grep the consumer docs for status-transition language ('mark as fixed', 'update status to') -- its presence means the store is living state, not a log.
